title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (Food and Health)

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) | Part 1.1 - level A1-A2 - scored items 1-3.

Level A1-A2. Three short questions about you and your interests, asked one after another. You have 30 seconds to answer each question. There is no preparation time. Begin speaking when you hear the sound.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) - PART 1.1

[EXAMINER: check the candidate's name and ID, then read the opening script aloud at a natural pace. Do not paraphrase. Three questions, asked one after another. 30 seconds for each answer. NO preparation time.]

EXAMINER (opening, read exactly): "Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[Play the chime, or say "beep" clearly, before each question. Start the 30-second timer the moment the candidate begins.]

QUESTION 1 (30 seconds): "What did you have for breakfast this morning?"

[At 30 seconds: "Thank you." Move straight on. Do not comment on the answer.]

QUESTION 2 (30 seconds): "Who usually cooks the meals in your home?"

[At 30 seconds: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 3 (30 seconds): "What do you do to stay healthy?"

[At 30 seconds: "Thank you." Do NOT announce an end here and do not pause: Part one point two follows immediately, and the opening script has already told the candidate that photographs are coming.]

[EXAMINER NOTE: these three answers are scored together as items 1-3, band 0-5. Ask only what is written. If the candidate is silent for more than 10 seconds, repeat the question once, word for word, and let the timer keep running.]

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) | Part 1.2 - level B1 - scored items 4-6.

Level B1. Two photographs on one theme and three questions, asked one after another. Question 4 (comparing the two pictures) has 45 seconds; questions 5 and 6 have 30 seconds each. There is no preparation time.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) - PART 1.2

[EXAMINER: show the candidate the two photographs side by side. If no photographs are available in Test bazasi, read the two descriptions below aloud, slowly, before asking Question 4. Questions are asked one after another. NO preparation time.]

[PICTURE 1: a family of five sitting around a small kitchen table on a Sunday afternoon, sharing a home-cooked meal - a large dish of rice and vegetables in the middle, a teapot, a plate of sliced tomatoes and fresh bread; a grandmother is passing a bowl to a child; everyone is talking and nobody is holding a phone; warm daylight through a window behind them.]

[PICTURE 2: a young man in a work uniform standing alone at a bus stop in the evening, eating a burger and chips out of a paper box balanced on one hand while scrolling his phone with the other; a plastic bottle of fizzy drink is on the bench beside him; traffic and bright shop signs behind him; he is looking at the screen, not at the food.]

EXAMINER (read exactly): "Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

[Play the chime. QUESTION 4 - 45 SECONDS. This is the compare and describe question. Start the timer when the candidate begins. At 45 seconds say "Thank you."]

[Play the chime. QUESTION 5 - 30 SECONDS:] "Which of these two meals do you think is better for a person's health, and why?"

[At 30 seconds: "Thank you."]

[Play the chime. QUESTION 6 - 30 SECONDS:] "Do you think it matters whether people eat together or alone? Why?"

[At 30 seconds: "Thank you. That is the end of Part one."]

[EXAMINER NOTE: these three answers are scored together as items 4-6, band 0-5. The candidate is expected to describe, give a personal opinion and justify it. Do not help the candidate find vocabulary and do not add your own opinion.]

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) | Part 2 - level B2 - scored item 7.

Level B2. One picture and three questions, all shown at the same time. You have 1 minute to think, then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. You are NOT required to describe the picture - it is only there to introduce the topic.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) - PART 2

[EXAMINER: show the picture and the three questions to the candidate AT THE SAME TIME. If no photograph is available in Test bazasi, read the description below aloud. Then give exactly 1 MINUTE of silent preparation, then 2 MINUTES for all three questions together.]

EXAMINER (read exactly): "Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

[PICTURE: a busy city street at lunchtime. Along one side there is a row of brightly lit fast-food windows with queues of office workers and students; squeezed between two of them is a small greengrocer's stall with crates of apples, carrots and greens, and an older shopkeeper standing beside it with no customers. People are walking past the stall towards the queues, several of them holding phones and paper cups.]

EXAMINER: "You do not have to describe the picture. The picture is only there to help you think about the topic. Here are your three questions."

THE THREE QUESTIONS (show them together and read them aloud once):
 1. Tell me about a change you have made to the way you eat or the way you exercise.
 2. How has that change affected your daily life?
 3. What do you think influences people's food choices most in general?

[Start the 1-minute preparation now. Say: "You have one minute. Your time starts now." The candidate may make notes. Stay silent.]

[At one minute: "Your preparation time is over." Play the chime. Start the 2-minute timer when the candidate begins speaking.]

[Timing reminders for the examiner only - do not interrupt the candidate: at 1 minute 30 seconds check that the candidate has reached the third question; if the candidate stops early and stays silent for more than 15 seconds, say once: "Is there anything else you would like to add?" Say nothing further.]

[At 2 minutes: "Thank you. That is the end of Part two."]

[EXAMINER NOTE: Part two is scored as item 7, band 0-5. The candidate is not required to describe the picture; do not deduct marks for ignoring it. The answer should move from personal experience to a general, reasoned judgement, with advantages and drawbacks weighed and justified.]

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) | Part 3 - level C1 - scored item 8.

Level C1. One topic statement with a FOR list of three points and an AGAINST list of three points. You choose TWO points from each list and give a balanced argument representing both sides. You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to speak. This is the final part of the test.

EXAMINER MARKING NOTE - official scoring split for the whole Speaking paper:
 items 1-3 (Part 1.1, all three answers together) = 0-5
 items 4-6 (Part 1.2, all three answers together) = 0-5
 item 7 (Part 2) = 0-5
 item 8 (Part 3) = 0-6
 Maximum raw score = 21. The raw score is converted to a rating out of 75.

 21=75, 20.5=73, 20=71, 19.5=69, 19=67, 18.5=65, 18=64, 17.5=63, 17=61, 16.5=59, 16=57, 15.5=56, 15=54, 14.5=52, 14=51, 13.5=50, 13=49, 12.5=47, 12=46, 11.5=45, 11=43, 10.5=42, 10=40, 9.5=39, 9=38, 8.5=37, 8=35, 7.5=33, 7=32, 6.5=30, 6=29, 5.5=27, 5=26, 4.5=24, 4=23, 3.5=21, 3=19, 2.5=17, 2=15, 1.5=13, 1=11, 0.5=10, 0=0

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant D (theme: food and health) - PART 3

[EXAMINER: show the topic statement and the two lists on the screen or on a printed card. Give exactly 1 MINUTE of silent preparation, then 2 MINUTES of speaking.]

EXAMINER (read exactly): "Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

TOPIC STATEMENT (show and read aloud):
 "Governments should put a high tax on sugary drinks and fast food."

FOR (read the three points aloud):
 1. Higher prices reduce how much unhealthy food people buy, and diet-related illness falls with it.
 2. The money raised can pay for hospitals, school meals and sports facilities.
 3. Manufacturers change their recipes to avoid the tax, so the whole food supply becomes healthier.

AGAINST (read the three points aloud):
 1. The tax hits low-income families hardest, because cheap food is the food they depend on.
 2. What a person eats is a private decision, not something the state should price.
 3. People simply switch to other unhealthy products, or buy them elsewhere, so consumption barely changes.

EXAMINER: "Choose two points from the 'for' list and two points from the 'against' list. You have one minute to prepare. Your time starts now."

[Silent preparation - 1 minute. The candidate may make notes. Stay silent.]

[At one minute: "Your preparation time is over." Play the chime. Start the 2-minute timer when the candidate begins.]

[Timing reminders for the examiner only: do not interrupt. If the candidate stops before 2 minutes and is silent for more than 15 seconds, say once: "Would you like to add anything for the other side?" Nothing further.]

[At 2 minutes: "Thank you. That is the end of the Speaking test."]

[EXAMINER NOTE: Part three is scored as item 8, band 0-6. A candidate who argues only one side cannot reach the top of the band, however fluent the English. Check that at least two points from each list are actually used.]
